answer: An agent economy can make each extra identity cost more than the last: the fee to register a new agent rises with every identity already tied to the same operator, so the first fake is cheap and the hundredth is ruinous, and the price ripples outward to any cluster sharing attestors. Newcomers harbor no standing until they earn it line by line, like a sonnet composed over many epochs of honest work, so a flood of fresh faces arrives voiceless and stays that way until each one proves itself separately.
